text: That afternoon: Holmes says that he and Watson must spend the night in her room
why: Holmes says this at ¶178, during the afternoon visit to Stoke Moran that Helen and Holmes arranged for early afternoon.

text: What will happen in the middle room to-night?
why: Holmes has just said they must spend the night in her room, and she is now sleeping in the middle room (¶134); a plain question the story raises.

text: What will happen in the middle room to-night? — the whistle comes, and something passes through the ventilator to the bed
id: q.tonight=the whistle comes, and something passes through the ventilator to the bed
why: A reasonable possibility from what has been shown: the whistle preceded Julia's death and recurred last night, and the ventilator links to the Doctor's room with the dummy rope running from it to the pillow. It names no specific agent.

text: What will happen in the middle room to-night? — nothing: Dr. Roylott lies low now that Holmes is on to him
id: q.tonight=nothing: Dr. Roylott lies low now that Holmes is on to him
why: Roylott confronted Holmes and knows he is interested in his affairs, so it is a fair possibility that he would hold back.

text: What will happen in the middle room to-night? — Dr. Roylott tries to get at her by open violence
id: q.tonight=Dr. Roylott tries to get at her by open violence
why: Roylott's violence is well established and Holmes himself anticipates it ('If he is violent', ¶131), so this is a fair possibility.
